narrative.overview: KnifeForge Pro should feel like a knifemaker's workshop notebook: a technical record kept by a craftsman. The notebook is technical first: numbers, drawings and dimensions are always legible, aligned and unambiguous. The artisan warmth lives at the edges. The current implementation is the notebook's sober base: a neutral cool-slate interface on stock Tailwind values, with flat white cards and one provisional indigo accent.
keyCharacteristics: Flat white sheets on a pale bench, separated by hairline borders, never by shadows.
One action accent (indigo, provisional), used for primary actions, active navigation and selection.
Small type (14 px body, 12 px labels).
Colour on the drawing is semantic: each layer role has a fixed stroke colour and dash pattern.

rules.name: The Layer Colour Is Meaning Rule
rules.body: On the drawing and client plan, a stroke's colour and dash identify its layer role. Never reuse them decoratively.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Indigo is the only accent. Status colours speak only for state.

rules.name: The Small And Exact Rule
rules.body: Body 14 px, labels 12 px, never below 12 px. Dimensions are never truncated or rounded for display beyond their stored precision.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the page flow casts a shadow; only dialogs and menus do. Use a hairline border to separate.

dos: Do separate surfaces with the 1 px Hairline border on white Paper over the Bench.
Do keep one primary indigo button per form or toolbar.
Do put labels above fields in 12 px Slate Muted, with 8 px as the default gap.
Do respect the layer colour code on the drawing and the client plan.
Do bring the carnet warmth through voice, material naming and notes first.
donts: Don't add shadows to cards, panels, buttons or inputs.
Don't introduce a second accent colour, or use red, green or amber decoratively.
Don't reuse layer colours for interface chrome inside the editor.
Don't set any text below 12 px, and never display a dimension rounded beyond its stored precision.
Don't treat the indigo as a brand commitment.
